stem: Birgitte has a six-sided dice. She suspects that the dice is biased so that the probability, $p$, that it will show a six on one throw is less than $\frac{1}{6}$. She throws the dice 30 times and finds that it shows a six on exactly 2 throws.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Use a binomial distribution with a 5% significance level to test Birgitte’s suspicion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Later, Birgitte carries out a similar test at the 5% significance level, using another 30 throws of the dice.
parts.text: Calculate the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Given that the value of $p$ is actually 0.02, calculate the probability of a Type II error.
